# @rxova/react-date-input

> A headless, accessible date field for React: segmented, keyboard-first, ordered
> by locale through `Intl`, with no calendar popup and no date library. The value
> is a `YYYY-MM-DD` string in and out — never a `Date`, which would drag a
> timezone into a calendar date. Zero runtime dependencies. No stylesheet.

## Install

    npm install @rxova/react-date-input

`react >= 18` is the only peer dependency.

## Minimal working example

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { DateInput } from '@rxova/react-date-input'

export function Birthday() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState<string | null>(null)

  return <DateInput label="Date of birth" value={value} onChange={setValue} max="2026-07-29" />
}
```

Segment order, separators and month names follow the locale:

```tsx
import { DateInput } from '@rxova/react-date-input'

export function Examples() {
  return (
    <>
      <DateInput label="US" locale="en-US" />
      <DateInput label="UK" locale="en-GB" />
      <DateInput label="Japan" locale="ja-JP" />
    </>
  )
}
```

`onChange` fires only when the date becomes complete and valid (or stops being
so). For every keystroke, use `onPartsChange`.

## Props

`<DateInput>` — the full surface is `DateInputProps` in the published types.

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| null` | — | Controlled `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `null` for empty. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| null` | — | Uncontrolled initial value. Ignored when `value` is set. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string \| null) => void` | — | Fires on complete/valid, and when that stops. Never mid-entry. |
| `onPartsChange` | `(parts: DateParts) => void` | — | Every keystroke, including while incomplete. |
| `min` | `string` | — | Earliest allowed date, inclusive, `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `max` | `string` | — | Latest allowed date, inclusive, `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `emitOutOfRange` | `boolean` | `true` | Reports an out-of-range date and marks the field invalid, rather than discarding it. |
| `locale` | `string` | the runtime's locale | BCP 47 tag deciding segment order, separators and month names. |
| `placeholders` | `DatePlaceholders` | `dd` / `mm` / `yyyy` | Per-segment placeholder text. |
| `segmentLabels` | `DateSegmentLabels` | `Day` / `Month` / `Year` | Per-segment accessible name. |
| `renderSegment` | `(state: DateSegmentState) => ReactNode` | — | Custom rendering for one segment. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — | Accessible name for the whole field. |
| `className` | `string` | — | |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | — | |
| `name` | `string` | — | Emits a hidden input carrying the ISO value, readable by a native `<form>`. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | inherited | Lays the field out; segment order still comes from `locale`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Sets `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid` on the group. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | — | ids of external error/help text. |
| `id` | `string` | — | Base id; segments derive `${id}-day`, `${id}-month`, `${id}-year`. |
| `onBlur` | `(event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | — | Fires when focus leaves the field, never between segments. |
| `onFocus` | `(event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | — | |
| `onWarn` | `(warning: DateWarning) => void` | `console.warn` | Development-only notice that a prop was coerced. Stripped from production builds. |

Also exported: the `useDateInput` hook, the segment helpers `segmentOrder`,
`datePieces`, `monthNames`, and the pure date functions `toISO`, `fromISO`,
`compareISO`, `withinRange`, `daysInMonth`, `isLeapYear`, plus `MIN_YEAR` and
`MAX_YEAR`.

## Styling

There is no stylesheet. Set CSS custom properties on any ancestor:
`--rx-date-gap`, `--rx-date-segment-padding`, `--rx-date-segment-radius`,
`--rx-date-literal-opacity`, `--rx-date-focus-ring`,
`--rx-date-focus-ring-offset`.

The focused segment paints a ring by default (`2px solid Highlight`), because a
`<span role="spinbutton">` gets none from the browser. Restyle it through those
two properties rather than removing it.

Or target the `data-*` attributes, which are public API covered by semver:
`data-rx-date-root`, `data-rx-date-segment` (`day` / `month` / `year`), `data-rx-date-value`,
plus the state hooks `data-complete`, `data-out-of-range`, `data-placeholder`,
`data-focused`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-invalid`.

## Three mistakes to avoid

1. **Converting the value to a `Date` on the way in or out.** `new Date('2026-01-01')`
   parses as UTC midnight and renders as the previous day anywhere west of it.
   Keep the `YYYY-MM-DD` string; `compareISO` and `withinRange` are exported so
   you rarely need anything else.
2. **Expecting `onChange` on every keystroke.** It fires when the date is complete
   and real, so you never receive `2026-02-3` half-typed. Subscribe to
   `onPartsChange` if you need the in-progress state.
3. **Hard-coding the segment order.** The order, the separators and the month
   names come from `Intl` for the given `locale` — a layout that assumes
   day-month-year is wrong in the US, and one that assumes three segments in a
   fixed order is wrong in ja-JP.
